novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 (thm:known-propensity-rate)
novelty_flags.one_line: With e supplied, W=(A-e(X))Y/[e(X)(1-e(X)) has regression mean τ with bounded nondegenerate noise, so the stated Hölder L2 detection rate is a standard goodness-of-fit benchmark rather than a new causal theorem.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies L2 testing of a smooth function against zero in Gaussian white noise and records the nonadaptive smoothness-s rate ε^(4s/(4s+1)); with ε=n^(-1/2), this is n^(-2s/(4s+1)).

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Demote the known-propensity rate to an explicitly cited benchmark lemma, and state the reduction from the known-e pseudo-outcome experiment to classical regression goodness-of-fit rather than presenting it as a novelty-bearing theorem.

For the complete-frontier question, record the first nonmatching likelihood moment and an explicit admissible bump/prior family in the α=β=1/10, d=γ=1 diagnostic regime before extrapolating the all-regime converse.
Add a compact primary-source comparison table separating the target class, null, separation metric, and finite-sample guarantee from KBRW, NBW, Dukes et al., PCM, and Yu.

recommended_next_step: Revise the oracle-rate node into a cited standard benchmark, then advance the field-grade sharp observational frontier and its legal null-supported converse to Stage 0.
